doc.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]

title: The future of jazz and the return of dance
summary: Person foresees a revolution as swing dancing brings back big bands and college swing groups.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Do you see a good future for this music in general, for jazz? I see so much publicity about it but I don’t see it transferred to live venues.

Well I see a future, I really do. Because I think there’s going to be I should say evolution but a revolution. You see part of it now would be kids starting the swing dancing things, suddenly you’re pushing bands back. Even if it’s Glenn Miller, Benny Goodman, and all those people, Count Basie and Duke Ellington, listen to those regularly as kids are starting to listen to that, in that swing dance situation. So then you’ll have groups, college groups, having swing bands. And it will evolve, it will go all the way around full circle again. And yeah I see a future, because I think that, as I said before, the dance will come back, as we see it is. And they should take a cue from Lincoln Center and the response that they had with it.
So people can get involved, as you said.
Yeah you’ve got to get people back into it. That’s what you’ve got to do.
